diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, $(f, g) = \int_\gamma f(w)\overline{g(w)}\,|dw|$ is the canonical inner-product on $L_2(\gamma)$ with corresponding norm $\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_2$.

issues.failure_explanation:
With the paper's linear-in-the-first-variable inner product, (f, \overline{i
u \psi}) = \int_\gamma f(i
u \psi)\,|dw|, whereas (\overline{i
u f}, \psi) = \int_\gamma \overline{i
u f}\,\overline{\psi}\,|dw|. These are not equal. Replacing f by \overline{i
u f} in the displayed estimate produces bilinear pairings of the form \int_\gamma f\psi\,|dw|, not the Hilbert-space coefficients (f, \psi). Thus the proof establishes, at best, a frame bound for reflected/conjugated coefficient functionals, not for the stated Lusin wavelet family {\psi_j^\pm} together with {w^{-j}}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove that the stated Hilbert-space family {\psi_j^\pm}\cup{w^{-j}} satisfies the frame bounds, or replace the theorem statement by the family for which the Cauchy-derivative discretization is actually valid and then rederive the Hardy-space frames.
issues.overall_effect: The central Lusin frame theorem for L_2(\gamma) and the derived Hardy-space frames are not established as stated. All later arguments that use the frame {\psi_j^+} to solve the Neumann problem inherit this gap.
issues.title: Main Lusin frame proof converts Cauchy-derivative coefficients to the wrong Hilbert-space frame vectors
issues.why_classification: The defect defeats the main theorem as stated and no source-supported comparable replacement of the stated frame family is provided; repairing it requires a new nontrivial frame argument rather than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposed exterior function g is intended to make the k-th derivative of its Cauchy integral equal to (1-q_0z^{-1})F^{(k)}. The displayed Laurent expression for G does not have this k-th derivative when k \ge 2. For example, with k=2 the lower-order Leibniz terms from differentiating (1-q_0z^{-1})F are not fully cancelled by the term kq_0z^{k-1}\int^\cdot z^{-k-1}F(z)\,dz. The construction works for k=1, but the proposition is stated for general k and is later used for general k.

issues.overall_effect: The proposition is not proved for k \ge 2. Since the removal lemma and the finite-\delta case of the Lusin frame theorem use the proposition to justify finite removal of Lusin wavelets, those results are also unsupported for k \ge 2.

issues.failure_explanation: The theoretical frame argument supplies a sufficient smallness threshold \varepsilon_0, and the displayed choice in the proof is \varepsilon_0 \le 1/20. The numerical section then uses \varepsilon=0.3, which is not shown to satisfy the required \varepsilon \le \varepsilon_0 condition. In addition, the formal results are infinite-dimensional frame statements; the paper does not prove convergence or stability of the finite truncated boundary-element system actually implemented, yet the abstract and numerical prose describe the method as enabling numerically stable approximation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\mathcal{L}^2\varepsilon \leq 1/4$, then $\{\rho(x_j)\}_{j = 1}^\infty$ is a Whitney set for $\rho(\cup_{j = 1}^\infty B_j)$ with respect to $\rho(A)$, with parameters $(\mathcal{L}^2\varepsilon, N)$, where $N \leq 4^n \mathcal{L}^{3n+1}\sigma$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a bi-Lipschitz map \rho with constant \mathcal{L}, the correct lower volume distortion bound is m(\rho(E_j)) \ge \mathcal{L}^{-n} m(E_j), not \mathcal{L}^{-1} m(E_j). The displayed inequality is false already for n=2 and a dilation by \mathcal{L}^{-1}. Consequently the derived covering constant 4^n \mathcal{L}^{3n+1}\sigma is not justified; the argument needs a larger power of \mathcal{L}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the volume estimate to use \mathcal{L}^{-n}m(E_j) and replace the covering constant by the resulting larger power of \mathcal{L}; this preserves the existence of an explicit Whitney set with a finite L-dependent covering constant.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the explicit Whitney set construction in the example is defective as written. The existence claim can still hold with a different L-dependent covering constant, but the stated constant and proof are not valid.
issues.title: Bi-Lipschitz Whitney lemma uses an incorrect volume distortion bound
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant-correction in a supporting lemma; it does not change the existence of Whitney sets or the main frame construction, only the quantitative L-dependence in the proof.
